name: molvic
author: shops-money-swapping
description:
molvic v2 (direction: shops, money and swapping) - THE SHOP SHELVES AND THE GOODS THAT GO
BACK WHERE THEY BELONG. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

WHY v2 (see challenges/lab/NOTES_shops.md, 2026-09-05). In lad-durnel-v2-1 both Opus players
finished molvic v1 at 100 %/100 % WITHOUT a demo: the edit (swap two letters) was guessable from
the picture, so the `n swap` checksum let the rule be found offline against ~55 harvested clues
("N = number of mutual pairs in the same column, verified 56/56"). durnel v1 failed the same way
and was fixed the same way: make the EDIT need the demo, and plant an exception so the natural
blind rule no longer reproduces the caption.

CLUE = THE SHELF UNIT DRAWN FROM THE FRONT, plus one caption line "<n> home".
  4 shelves (was 5). Each shelf is a row "|X X   X Y X ...|" of 9-12 slots (one character per
  slot, separated by a space); under each shelf row is its edge "+-----+". A slot holds a good
  (a capital letter, one letter per kind) or is an empty gap " ".
  A SHELF BELONGS to the letter most of its goods are (margin >= 2 on every row of every clue).
  A STRAY is a good standing on somebody else's shelf: 5-8 of them (was 7-14), at most 3 on a
  shelf, never two of the same kind on one shelf. ONE OR TWO SHELVES ARE FULL (no gap at all);
  every other shelf has 2-3 gaps. Clue 166-198 chars, 8 lines + caption.

ANSWER = THE CLUE'S PICTURE WITH THOSE n GOODS PUT AWAY. Exactly 2n characters change: each
mover's old slot becomes a gap and the first gap on its own shelf becomes its shelf's letter.
Nothing else changes. The answer is UNIQUE per clue. The trailing "<n> home" line may be kept or
dropped; both score 1 (house rule 2026-09-05). Trailing spaces and trailing newlines are ignored.

RULE (one breath): TWO GOODS THAT STAND IN LINE - the same slot, one above the other - AND ARE
EACH ON THE OTHER'S SHELF BOTH GO HOME, AND A GOOD GOES HOME INTO THE FIRST EMPTY SLOT ON ITS OWN
SHELF; IF ITS OWN SHELF IS FULL THERE IS NOWHERE TO PUT IT, SO IT STAYS WHERE IT IS. Formally: a
good of kind H[k] at (row i, slot j) moves iff the good at (row k, slot j) is of kind H[i] AND
row k contains a gap; it is erased from (i,j) and written into the first gap of row k (the gap
positions are read off the CLUE, before anything moves). n counts the goods that move, so the two
pictures differ in exactly 2n characters. generate() never lets two movers want the same shelf.

WHAT CHANGED FROM v1, AND WHY IT IS THE fennick SHAPE
  (a) THE EDIT IS NO LONGER GUESSABLE. In v1 the two goods swapped cells, so a player who had the
      rule could draw the answer. Now each good is erased and redrawn in the FIRST GAP of its own
      shelf - a slot the caption says nothing about, usually far from the column it stood in
      (82 % of movers land to the LEFT of their old column). The blind rendering ("they swap over
      where they stand") scores 0.0 %.
  (b) THE NATURAL BLIND RULE IS NOW WRONG. Because a good needs somewhere to land, a FULL shelf
      refuses it. Every clue plants an in-line mutual pair whose good has no room (100 %,
      audited over 4000 clues), so v1's rule - the one both players deduced offline - reproduces
      the caption on 0.0 % of clues instead of 100 %. Offline hypothesis testing now falsifies
      the first sensible reading; with a demo the checksum is a full verifier again.
  (c) THE JUDGE'S NOTE (kid 3.67: "the picture is dense, 7-14 strays across 5 shelves, the swap
      signal is buried"): 4 shelves, 5-8 strays, and the only thing that ever happens is in a
      column where two strays stand one above the other. No count-based crack was opened: see
      the witness table (every count/position template is at or under the 12 % foothold).

OFFLINE CHECKSUM TEST (1200 clues; what fraction of clues each COUNT hypothesis reproduces)
  in-line mutual goods with room at home (TRUE)                          100.0 %
  in-line mutual pairs                                                    30.8 %
  in-line mutual pairs with room for both                                 11.8 %
  in-line mutual goods, room ignored (v1's rule, the players' reading)      0.0 %
  mutual goods, alignment ignored / strays in line / strays with room       0.0 %
An exhaustive search over conjunctions of nine natural per-stray predicates finds only two rules
that reproduce the caption everywhere: the true one, and its TWIN "in line, mutual, and the shelf
it is STANDING on is not full" - which per pair always counts the same but picks the other good
of the pair, and cannot be drawn (it would send a good to a full shelf). The twin is
indistinguishable from the caption alone and is settled by one look at a demo (12.2 % either way).

EVERY DEMO TEACHES THE WHOLE RULE. generate() plants, in every instance (audited, 4000 clues):
  P1  an in-line mutual good whose own shelf is FULL, so it stays        100 %
  P2  a mutual pair that is NOT in line, so neither moves                100 %
  P3  a third stray standing in a going-home column, whose own shelf HAS
      room -> kills "anything in line with a stray goes home"            100 %
  P4  a stray standing on a FULL shelf with room at home, that stays
      -> kills "the goods on the packed shelf get put away"              100 %
  P5  a stray with a GAP in line on its own shelf -> kills "it goes back
      if there is a space for it right there"                            100 %
  P6  every mover's home shelf has 2-3 gaps, and in every clue at least
      one mover's landing gap is neither the nearest gap to its column
      nor the nearest gap on its left -> "the FIRST gap" is forced       100 %
  P7  the movers are never simply the first n strays in reading order    100 %
  P8  for n >= 2, some movers climb and some are lifted down             100 %
  Configurations (4 shelves, F = full): n=0 [F=a,b; pair (a,b)]; n=1 [F=a; (a,b)] or
  [F=a,b; (a,b),(a,c)]; n=2 [F=a,b; (a,c),(b,d)]; n=3 [F=a; (a,b),(c,d)].

THE FOOTHOLD (lever 7). 12.2 % of clues say "0 home": nothing moves and the correct answer IS the
clue returned unchanged, caption kept or dropped. Those clues look exactly like the others - they
still carry an in-line mutual pair (both of whose shelves are full), a mutual pair out of line,
strays in line - so a demo-less player who reads "a shelf unit, things in the wrong place,
2 home" and echoes the picture scores ~12 %, and so does every count-based guess. What the clue
alone reveals about the answer's SHAPE: it is this same shelf picture with a few goods put away,
and the caption says how many go - so a demo-less player always has a well-formed attempt.

WITNESS TABLE (1500 fresh clues, shipped scorer. Templates render with the TRUE drawing
convention - a player who has seen a demo and holds the wrong rule - unless marked BLIND):
  BLIND: in-line mutual pairs swapped in place (v1's rule + v1's edit)     0.0 %  <- was 100 %
  BLIND: the same, only the pairs with room, swapped in place            12.3 %
  BLIND: in-line mutual goods rubbed out                                  0.0 %
  BLIND: tidy up - every stray put right where it stands                  0.0 %
  clue returned unchanged                                                12.3 %  <- the foothold
  clue unchanged, caption dropped                                        12.3 %
  only the good on the LOWER shelf of each pair goes home                20.7 %  <- the top rival
  only the good on the UPPER shelf of each pair goes home                19.9 %
  n strays at random go home                                             16.1 %
  every in-line mutual good goes home (fullness ignored)                  0.0 %
  the whole pair goes home if either of the two has room                 12.3 %
  TWIN rule (the good on a shelf that has room), moved / swapped         12.3 %
  true movers -> the LAST gap / the nearest gap / the nearest gap left   12.3 % each
  true movers -> the first gap on the shelf they were standing on        12.3 %
  true movers, old slot filled by the partner (swap AND move)            12.3 %
  true movers, old slot filled by the shelf's letter                     12.3 %
  true movers copied home, old slot left as it was                       12.3 %
  true movers rubbed out, never arriving                                 12.3 %
  true movers, and the refused goods vanish too                           0.0 %
  a good needs a gap IN LINE at home                                     12.3 %
  any stray with a gap on its own shelf goes home                         0.0 %
  any stray in line with another stray goes home                          0.0 %
  any mutual stray (alignment ignored) goes home                          0.0 %
  any stray on a FULL shelf with room at home goes home                   0.0 %
  the first n strays in reading order / the strays on the fullest shelf  12.3 / 6.4 %
  one fixed real answer for every clue / demo replay                      0.0 %
  TRUE RULE (solve), caption kept / dropped / rows padded               100.0 %
No template beats 21 %. The two that pay are the pair-half guesses (which of the two goods in a
one-sided pair moves), and they are a coin flip only on the n=1 clues; one demo settles them.

WELL-FORMEDNESS (14 attacks x 1500 clues, all 0.0 %): gaps drawn as dots, lowercased, shelf edges
removed, slot spacing squeezed out, rows reversed, caption count changed, the answer sent twice, a
junk line appended, half the picture, the caption alone, the empty string, 4000 chars of junk, one
fixed answer, another clue's answer. Declared leniencies: trailing newlines, trailing whitespace
on any row, caption present or absent. The scorer rebuilds the whole expected picture from the
clue and compares line by line, so nothing about the rule can be smuggled through the form.
Uniqueness: 15 390 single-character mutations of true answers, 0 still scored 1.

ENGINEERING (4000 fresh seeds). generate mean 0.34 ms, p99 1.26 ms, max 4.1 ms, 0 fallback uses,
2000/2000 clues distinct and deterministic (identical output under four PYTHONHASHSEEDs); solve
0.012 ms; score 0.014 ms on real answers and 0.015 ms on 4000-char junk. Scorer 494/512 chars,
solve 1077/5000, generate 8.0k/50000, clue and solution 166-198/1024. n is 0 (12.2 %), 1 (15 %),
2 (21 %) or 3 (51 %). An independent re-implementation (Counter majority, picture rebuilt from
scratch) agreed with solve/score on 1200/1200 clues.

INTENDED SPLIT. With a demo: the pictures differ in 2n characters that come in pairs - a good
gone from one row, a gap filled on another - so "it has been put away on its own shelf" is the
first thing a player sees; which gap is forced by P6, and the good that DIDN'T move (P1) is
standing over a shelf with no gaps at all. Without a demo: the caption says goods go home, so the
natural reading is "the two in each other's places trade back" - which is v1's rule with v1's
edit, and it now scores 0.0 %; the honest blind attempt is to echo the picture, which pays 12 %.
The residual risk is a theorist who both finds the count rule offline (it needs two conjuncts,
one of which - "there is room at home" - only makes sense once you believe the good MOVES) and
then buys the landing convention with live probes; durnel v2 carries the same risk and held at
10 % blind.

LEVERS. Too easy: (a) require the caption dropped (removes the identity foothold and the offline
checksum); (b) draw the goods as two-character tokens so the slot grid has to be parsed;
(c) let a shelf be full on one side only (a good goes to the first gap AFTER its own column).
Too hard: (a) drop the full-shelf clause, so every in-line mutual good goes home (measured: the
caption is then reproduced by the pair count, which is most of the way back to v1);
(b) draw one good already put away in the clue as a worked instance; (c) always give a mover's
shelf exactly one gap, so "the first gap" is "the gap".
generate:
# THE SHOP SHELVES AND THE GOODS THAT GO BACK WHERE THEY BELONG.
# 4 shelf rows of slots; a shelf belongs to the letter most of its goods are. A STRAY is a good
# standing on somebody else's shelf. Caption "<n> home": n goods go home. Two goods that stand
# IN LINE (the same slot, one above the other) and are EACH ON THE OTHER'S SHELF both go home,
# and a good goes home into the FIRST EMPTY SLOT on its own shelf, leaving its old slot empty.
# A FULL shelf (no empty slot at all) has no room, so a good whose own shelf is full stays put.
# Every clue plants: a good with no room at home, so it stays (kills "all the in-line pairs");
# a mutual pair NOT in line; a third stray in a going-home column whose own shelf HAS room;
# a stray on a full shelf that has room at home; a stray with a gap in line on its own shelf.
AL = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPRSTUVWY"
FB = ("|E E   G E E C E E  |\n+-------------------+\n|G G G G G P G G G E|\n"
      "+-------------------+\n|C C C C C C E C C C|\n+-------------------+\n"
      "|P     P P G E P P P|\n+-------------------+\n2 home")


def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    zero = r.random() < 0.12                     # decided once, before any retry
    for _ in range(500):
        W = r.randint(9, 11)                     # slots per shelf
        LT = r.sample(AL, 4)                     # what each shelf is for
        a, b, c, d = r.sample(range(4), 4)
        if zero:                                 # the only in-line pair is refused by two
            FUL, AM = [a, b], [(a, b)]           # full shelves, so nothing moves at all
        else:
            FUL, AM = r.choice([([a], [(a, b)]),                    # n=1
                                ([a, b], [(a, b), (a, c)]),        # n=1
                                ([a, b], [(a, c), (b, d)]),        # n=2
                                ([a, b], [(a, c), (b, d)]),
                                ([a, b], [(a, c), (b, d)]),
                                ([a, b], [(a, c), (b, d)]),
                                ([a], [(a, b), (c, d)]),           # n=3
                                ([a], [(a, b), (c, d)]),
                                ([a], [(a, b), (c, d)]),
                                ([a], [(a, b), (c, d)])])
        G = [[LT[i]] * W for i in range(4)]
        occ = [set() for _ in range(4)]

        def put(host, home, j):                  # a good of LT[home] left on shelf `host`
            G[host][j] = LT[home]
            occ[host].add(j)

        def free(*rows):
            return [j for j in range(W) if all(j not in occ[i] for i in rows)]

        def kinds(i):
            return [G[i][x] for x in occ[i]]

        ok = True
        cols = []
        for p, q in AM:                          # the in-line pairs: each on the other's shelf
            f = free(p, q)
            if not f:
                ok = False
                break
            j = r.choice(f)
            put(p, q, j)
            put(q, p, j)
            cols.append((j, p, q))
        if not ok:
            continue
        pm = [(p, q) for p in FUL for q in range(4)                 # plant: a mutual pair NOT in
              if q not in FUL and (p, q) not in AM and (q, p) not in AM]   # line - and the good
        r.shuffle(pm)                            # left on the full shelf DOES have room at home
        for p, q in pm[:1]:
            f1 = [x for x in free(p) if LT[q] not in kinds(p)]
            f2 = [x for x in free(q) if LT[p] not in kinds(q)]
            if not f1 or len(f2) < 2:
                ok = False
                break
            j1 = r.choice(f1)
            f2 = [x for x in f2 if x != j1]
            if not f2:
                ok = False
                break
            put(p, q, j1)
            put(q, p, r.choice(f2))
        if not ok or not pm or not cols:
            continue
        j, p, q = r.choice(cols)                 # plant: a third stray in a going-home column,
        opt = [(m, e) for m in range(4) if m not in (p, q) and j in free(m)   # standing there
               for e in range(4) if e != m and e not in FUL                   # with room at
               and G[e][j] != LT[m] and LT[e] not in kinds(m)]                # home, and staying
        if not opt:
            continue
        opt.sort(key=lambda t: (t[0] not in FUL, r.random()))
        m, e = opt[0]
        put(m, e, j)
        if r.random() < .5:                      # a lone stray for texture, standing pat
            lone = [(i, e, x) for i in range(4) for e in range(4) if e != i
                    for x in free(i) if G[e][x] != LT[i] and LT[e] not in kinds(i)]
            if lone:
                i, e, x = r.choice(lone)
                put(i, e, x)
        if max(len(o) for o in occ) > 3 or not 5 <= sum(len(o) for o in occ) <= 8:
            continue
        NF = [i for i in range(4) if i not in FUL]
        gap = {i: set() for i in NF}
        cand = [(k, x) for k in NF for x in range(W) if x not in occ[k]
                for i in range(4) if i != k and x in occ[i] and G[i][x] == LT[k]]
        if not cand:                             # plant: a stray with a gap in line on its own
            continue                             # shelf (there is room, but not in line)
        k, x = r.choice(cand)
        gap[k].add(x)
        for k in NF:
            f = [x for x in range(W) if x not in occ[k] and x not in gap[k]]
            need = r.randint(2, 3) - len(gap[k])
            if len(f) < need:
                ok = False
                break
            gap[k] |= set(r.sample(f, need))
        if not ok:
            continue
        for k in NF:
            for x in gap[k]:
                G[k][x] = " "
        st = [(i, x, LT.index(G[i][x])) for i in range(4) for x in sorted(occ[i])]
        mov = [(i, x, k) for i, x, k in st if G[k][x] == LT[i] and " " in G[k]]
        n = len(mov)
        if len({k for i, x, k in mov}) != n:      # two goods must never want the same gap
            continue
        if not [1 for i, x, k in st if G[k][x] == LT[i] and " " not in G[k]]:
            continue                             # plant: a good with no room at home, so it stays
        if not [1 for i, x, k in st if i in FUL and " " in G[k] and (i, x, k) not in mov]:
            continue                             # plant: a stray on a full shelf that has room
        if not [1 for i, x, k in st if (i, x, k) not in mov and " " in G[k]
                and any(m != i and G[m][x] not in (" ", LT[m]) for m in range(4))]:
            continue                             # plant: in line with a stray, room at home, stays
        gp = {i: [x for x in range(W) if G[i][x] == " "] for i in range(4)}
        if n and not [1 for i, x, k in mov
                      if gp[k][0] != min(gp[k], key=lambda y: abs(y - x))]:
            continue                             # the first gap is not the nearest gap
        if n and not [1 for i, x, k in mov if len([y for y in gp[k] if y < x]) > 1]:
            continue                             # nor the nearest gap on its left
        if n > 1 and len({i > k for i, x, k in mov}) < 2:
            continue                             # some goods climb, some are lifted down
        fst, seen = [], set()
        for i, x, k in st:                       # the movers are not simply the first n strays
            if len(fst) < n and k not in seen and " " in G[k]:
                seen.add(k)
                fst.append((i, x, k))
        if n and fst == mov:
            continue
        if any(sorted([G[i].count(y) for y in set(G[i]) - {" ", LT[i]}] + [0])[-1]
               > G[i].count(LT[i]) - 2 for i in range(4)):
            continue                             # the shelf's own letter wins by 2 or more
        bar = "+" + "-" * (2 * W - 1) + "+"
        out = []
        for i in range(4):
            out.append("|" + " ".join(G[i]) + "|")
            out.append(bar)
        return "\n".join(out) + "\n" + str(n) + " home"
    return FB
solve:
def solve(clue):
    P = clue.split("\n")
    T = P.pop()                                   # the "<n> home" caption, copied through
    R = [x[1::2] for x in P[::2]]                 # the slots of each shelf row
    H = [max(set(x) - {" "}, key=x.count) for x in R]         # what each shelf is for
    G = [list(x) for x in R]
    M = []
    for i, x in enumerate(R):
        for j, y in enumerate(x):
            if y != " " and y != H[i]:            # a good on somebody else's shelf
                k = H.index(y)
                if R[k][j] == H[i] and " " in R[k]:   # in line with one of its own shelf's goods
                    M.append((i, j, k))               # standing here, and there is room at home
    for i, j, k in M:
        G[i][j] = " "                             # it leaves the slot it was standing in
    for i, j, k in M:
        G[k][R[k].index(" ")] = H[k]              # and goes into the first gap on its own shelf
    E = ["|" + " ".join(g) + "|" for g in G]
    return "\n".join([P[i] if i % 2 else E[i // 2] for i in range(len(P))]) + "\n" + T
